e.etymology: From the Irish surname O Fallamhain, descendant of Fallamhan, a name meaning leader or ruler. It became a girls' name in the US through Fallon Carrington of the 1980s soap Dynasty.

assoc.t: Jimmy Fallon, Tonight Show host (surname)
Fallon Carrington of Dynasty

e.etymology: From Aramaic marta, lady or mistress. In the Gospels Martha is the sister of Mary and Lazarus, busy with serving while Mary listens to Jesus.

assoc.t: Martha Stewart, homemaking and media mogul
Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts island

e.etymology: The Old Norse spelling of Freya, from freyja, lady. Freyja is the Norse goddess of love, beauty and war.

assoc.t: Freyja, Norse goddess of love and war
Freya in the God of War video games

e.note: The j is said like a y, so many Americans will be unsure how to read or spell it.

e.etymology: A K- spelling of Casey, from the Irish surname O Cathasaigh, descendant of Cathasach, a name meaning vigilant. It also reads as the initials K.C.

assoc.t: Kacey Musgraves, country-pop singer

e.etymology: The Spanish form of Maurice, from Latin Mauricius, from Maurus, a Moor, a person from Mauretania. Saint Maurice was a 3rd-century Roman soldier and martyr.
namesakes: Mauricio Umansky (real estate broker, Real Housewives)
Mauricio Pochettino (soccer manager who coached the US men's team)

e.etymology: A modern elaboration of Ava with the Latinate ending -iana, sometimes linked to avian, of birds. Aviana is separately a Greenlandic name built on a word for family.
A modern American coinage built on Ray, in the style of Rylan and Braylon. It took off after 2010 with Raylan Givens, the U.S. marshal of the TV series Justified.
namesakes: Raylan Givens (U.S. marshal in the TV series Justified)

assoc.t: Raylan Givens, marshal in the TV series Justified

e.etymology: A short form of Finola, from Irish Fionnghuala, 'white shoulder'. In the US it has also been used as a feminine counterpart to Nolan.

assoc.t: NOLA, nickname for New Orleans, Louisiana

e.etymology: The Spanish and Italian form of Elisha, from Hebrew Elisha, 'my God is salvation', the prophet who succeeds Elijah in the Books of Kings.
From an English surname that began as a byname from Old English draca, 'dragon'. Some families took it from the word drake, a male duck.

assoc.t: Drake, Canadian rapper and singer
drake, the word for a male duck

e.meaning: house of figs, or house of affliction
e.etymology: From the New Testament village near Jerusalem where Lazarus, Mary and Martha lived. Its Aramaic name is read as 'house of affliction' or 'house of figs'; scholars disagree.
namesakes: Bethany Hamilton (surfer who survived a shark attack)
Bethany Joy Lenz (actress, One Tree Hill)

assoc.t: biblical village near Jerusalem, home of Lazarus

e.etymology: A short form of Christopher, Christian, Christina and Christine, all built on Greek Christos, 'anointed one'. It has long been given as a name in its own right.
The English word true, from Old English treowe, 'faithful, trustworthy', used as a virtue name. It is also an English surname. Khloe Kardashian chose it for her daughter in 2018.

assoc.t: True Jackson, VP, Nickelodeon sitcom heroine

e.meaning: maidens (the name of a bright star)
e.etymology: The name of a bright star in Canis Major, from Arabic al-adhara, 'the maidens'. As a given name it is used mostly in Spanish-speaking families.

assoc.t: Adhara, second-brightest star in Canis Major

e.etymology: From the laurel tree, Latin laurus, whose leaves crowned victors in ancient Greece and Rome. It is one of the plant names that came into use in the 19th century.

assoc.t: Laurel and Hardy, classic film comedy duo
Yanny or Laurel, viral audio clip of 2018
laurel wreath, ancient symbol of victory

e.meaning: gray battle (via Griselda); in Yiddish, blessed or happy
e.etymology: A short form of Griselda, a Germanic name read as 'gray battle'. A separate Yiddish Zelda is the feminine of Zelig, 'blessed, happy'.
namesakes: Zelda Fitzgerald (Jazz Age writer, wife of F. Scott Fitzgerald)
Princess Zelda (Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda)

assoc.t: The Legend of Zelda, Nintendo video game series

e.etymology: A modern American name that came into use in the 2010s alongside Kairo, Kylo and Kyrie. It has no settled meaning.
From Arabic ahmad, 'most praiseworthy', the superlative of hamid. It is one of the names of the Prophet Muhammad and is used across the Muslim world.
From Byzantine Greek kyra, 'lady', the name of a Greek Orthodox saint, or from Cyra, a feminine form of Cyrus. In English it is also used as a variant of Kira and Keira.
From an English surname. Its use as a first name, strongest in the American South, owes much to S. Truett Cathy, the founder of Chick-fil-A.

assoc.t: S. Truett Cathy, founder of Chick-fil-A

e.etymology: The name of an early martyr, shortened from Latin Christiana, 'Christian woman', which goes back to Greek Christos, 'anointed one'. A 17th-century queen of Sweden bore it.
From an English surname that probably goes back to the Old Norse name Thorsteinn, 'Thor's stone'. Actor Dustin Hoffman made it a familiar first name from the late 1960s.

assoc.t: Dustin, the curly-haired kid of Stranger Things

e.etymology: From Sanskrit arava, 'sound, cry', by way of Hindi. It rose sharply in India and among Indian American families in the 2000s.
e.note: Name sites often gloss it as 'peaceful'; the Sanskrit word means 'sound'.

e.etymology: From Old French Leonard, from Old High German leo, 'lion', and hart, 'hard, brave'. A 6th-century Frankish saint, patron of prisoners, spread the name.
namesakes: Leonard Nimoy (actor, Spock in Star Trek)

e.etymology: A Russian short form of Larissa, a name of Greek origin. It spread through the English-speaking world with the novel Doctor Zhivago (1957) and its 1965 film, whose heroine is Lara.
namesakes: Lara Croft (heroine of the Tomb Raider games and films)

assoc.t: Lara Croft, heroine of the Tomb Raider games

e.etymology: An elaboration of Coralie, itself from coral, first used for a character in Adolphe Adam's 1849 opera Le toreador. Neil Gaiman's 2002 novel Coraline and its 2009 film made it familiar.
namesakes: Coraline Jones (heroine of Neil Gaiman's Coraline)

assoc.t: Coraline, Neil Gaiman novel and 2009 stop-motion film

e.note: Often misheard or misread as Caroline.

e.etymology: From Arabic karim, 'generous, noble', from the verb karuma. Al-Karim, 'the Generous', is one of the names of God in Islam.
namesakes: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (NBA Hall of Fame center)

assoc.t: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, NBA legend known as Kareem

e.etymology: From an English place name and surname, Old English west and leah, 'western wood or clearing'. Westley is the farm boy hero of The Princess Bride.

assoc.t: Westley, hero of The Princess Bride

e.etymology: A modern American coinage in the family of Jabari, Jamari and Zakari, using the Ja- opening popular since the 1970s. It has no meaning of its own.
A spelling of Connor, the English form of Irish Conchobhar, 'lover of hounds', the name of a legendary king of Ulster. Conner is also an English occupational surname for an inspector.

assoc.t: the Conners, TV family of Roseanne and The Conners

e.etymology: A short form of Ezekiel, the Hebrew prophet whose name means 'God strengthens'. It is now often given as a name in its own right.
namesakes: Ezekiel Elliott (NFL running back known as Zeke)

e.etymology: A feminine spelling of Andy, in the US usually short for Andrea, the feminine of Andrew, from Greek andreios, 'manly, brave'. It is now often given as a full name.
namesakes: Andi Mack (title character of the Disney Channel series)
